Definition: from G4982; a deliverer, i.e. God or Christ:--saviour.
BiblicalUsage: The Saviour is born, believed, waited for, and testified to. Unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord; the Samaritans confess this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world; Titus looks for the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ; and John testifies that the Father sent the Son to be the Saviour of the world.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the title says it all: He came to save, and the world is what He came to save. I hold that no one who comes to Him is turned away, and the Saviour of the world is my Saviour too.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
